item.text:
**ACCEPT** for the targeted hook-bypass recheck. Each successful gate is followed by the native operation: write (`mod.rs:148–184`), file sync and checked close (`replace.rs:116–142`, `create_new.rs:79–105`), rename/link, unlink, and directory sync (`mod.rs:189–201`). The close gates borrow `&File`; the owned file is still consumed by `close_checked`.

The new successful-hook regressions assert target bytes, modes/inode, commit and durability flags, cleanup, and operation observations ([tests.rs:252](/Users/megasoft78/Desktop/Freelance/vexel/.worktrees/rust3-atomic-files/rust/crates/vexel-platform-macos/src/atomic_files/tests.rs:252), [tests.rs:425](/Users/megasoft78/Desktop/Freelance/vexel/.worktrees/rust3-atomic-files/rust/crates/vexel-platform-macos/src/atomic_files/tests.rs:425)). Failure paths retain precommit targets and clean temporary files; postcommit failures report committed state.

The eight existing native-service assertions remain present in the two crate unit tests and six `native_system` integration tests. The updated parity map documents the fault-gate adaptation and native operations. I did not run tests or builds; this is not a whole-application certification.
